newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgian diplomat to stay in U.S. during probe.
newsitem.headline: Georgian diplomat to stay in U.S. during probe.

text.p: Georgia said on Thursday it had agreed not to recall one of its diplomats, who was involved in a fatal car crash in Washington, before the result of an investigation by U.S. authorities.

Foreign Minister Irakly Menagarishvili told reporters in Tbilisi that his government had received a request from the U.S. State Department that the diplomat not be allowed to leave the United States before inquiries were completed.

Gueorgui Makharadze, 35, could face charges ranging from negligent homicide to second degree murder, which carries a sentence of 20 years to life, if the Georgian government agreed to waive his diplomatic immunity.
A 16-year old American girl, Joviane Waltrick of Maryland, died in the crash last Friday.

"We received a request from the U.S. State Department that Mr. Makharadze not leave the territory of the U.S. while the preliminary investigation is being completed. We will fulfill this request," Menagarishvili said.
The State Department has said it will ask Georgia to waive Makharadze's diplomatic immunity from prosecution if the investigation shows he committed a criminal act.
But officials say they do not expect Tbilisi to comply, in which case they will press for his withdrawal.
Menagarishvili, who called the accident a "tragedy", indicated Georgia would wait until the completion of the police work before deciding how Makharadze should be punished.

"We think a person should carry responsibility for their crimes. How and in what form a person should be punished we will work out on the basis of documents we hope to receive in the next few days," he said.
Kevin Ohlson, spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office in Washington, said on Wednesday that a preliminary investigation revealed "sufficient evidence that a criminal act was committed."
He noted that Makharadze appeared to have been speeding when the accident occurred and may have been under the influence of alcohol.

The case has caused an outcry in Washington over the whole concept of diplomatic immunity. Republican Senator Judd Gregg of New Hampshire on Monday urged President Bill Clinton to withhold aid to Georgia until it waived Makharadze's immunity.
